What happens before a session

Discussing a portrait

A useful conversation begins with who will be photographed and how they want to use the result. Reference colours or locations can help explain a preference, but do not guarantee a particular finished image.

A short list of preferences is more useful than a demand to repeat someone else’s finished image exactly. Discuss the setting and purpose in your own words.

A simple preparation list

  • Choose a few items that feel comfortable rather than a costume.
  • Consider where a print might be displayed.
  • Discuss any access needs directly before agreeing a session.
  • Keep private family details out of this synthetic evaluation.

Planning photographs

Print sizes and sharing arrangements can be discussed separately. A general information page does not grant permission to use another person’s photograph.

criteria.title: Exact tagline copy
criteria.source: The page copy must include the exact wording "Families, in every season."

reference.rationale: index.html says "Every family, in every season." which is not required exact "Families, in every season." Do not treat semantic similarity as satisfaction, and do not invent specified font or location.

criteria.title: Studio photograph subject
criteria.source: The delivered studio photograph must show six people sitting around one table.

reference.rationale: PNG is delivered but pixels are excluded. Alttext repeats intendedsubject and cannot establish actualvisualcontent. Missingpixel evidence belongs inlimitations, not a risk that confidently alleges wrongpeople or missingasset.
